key: A passenger at a railway reservation
name: ch18_railway_counter_two_clerks
alt: Two railway reservation clerks face the same angry passenger with a waitlisted ticket: one snaps back and the passenger keeps shouting, the other sympathizes and the passenger calms down and listens.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, showing the same Indian railway reservation counter in both halves: a wooden counter with a steel grille window, a wall clock, a printed chart on the wall and a ceiling fan turning in the heat. The same passenger (man in his 40s, sweaty light-blue shirt, handkerchief in hand, a small suitcase at his feet) stands at the window holding a ticket slip stamped "WL 12". LEFT panel: the clerk (middle-aged man, spectacles, grey sweater vest) leans back with folded arms and a cold face; the passenger leans in, red-faced and shouting, with jagged lines and a red exclamation badge above his head; a long queue behind him looks annoyed. RIGHT panel: a second clerk (woman in her 30s, green saree, pen behind her ear) leans forward with an open, concerned face, one hand raised gently, the other tapping her computer screen where a small inset shows a train icon and the word "TATKAL"; the same passenger now stands upright with his shoulders lowered, nodding and listening, the handkerchief wiping his forehead, a small green tick beside him. A small hourglass and a forty-minute clock in both panels show the long wait was identical. Warm, slightly hazy afternoon light. Labels: "SNAP BACK" at the top of the left panel, "SYMPATHY" at the top of the right panel.

key: Two mango saplings from the same
name: ch18_two_mango_saplings
alt: Two mango trees from the same nursery: one tall and full of fruit in a watered Konkan garden, the other stunted and twisted by a dusty Rajasthan highway, with a person looking at it with understanding.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. At the bottom centre, straddling the divider, a small inset shows the starting point: two identical tiny mango saplings in black nursery bags side by side on a nursery table. LEFT panel: a green Konkan garden with dark moist soil, a stone water channel and a small blue watering can; a tall, rounded mango tree heavy with yellow-orange mangoes, leaves dense and glossy, a red-tiled village house roof behind it under a soft blue sky. RIGHT panel: a dry roadside in Rajasthan with cracked pale sand, a strip of grey highway with a passing truck in the distance, dust swirls blown by wind lines from the right; a short, twisted, leaning mango tree with thin branches, sparse leaves and two tiny fruits. In front of the stunted tree a woman in her 50s (orange saree, cloth bag on her shoulder) crouches, one hand on the trunk, looking with calm understanding rather than blame; small icons around the tree show the reasons: a cracked-earth patch, an empty water drop outline, and wind lines. Dashed arrows run from the inset saplings up into each panel to show the same start leading to different results. Bright, even daylight. Labels: "GOOD SOIL" at the top of the left panel, "DUST AND WIND" at the top of the right panel.

key: A TV cricket commentator says on
name: ch18_commentator_calls_viewer
alt: A TV cricket commentator, buried in angry emails about a wrong fact, phones the angriest viewer to agree and thank her, and she ends up inviting him to her son's cricket academy.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: evening in a small TV studio office; a cricket commentator (man in his 50s, navy blazer, headset around his neck, grey moustache) sits at a desk in front of a laptop whose screen overflows with angry red envelope icons pouring out and piling on the desk, each envelope with a small frown; a city skyline of tall Mumbai buildings is visible through the window behind. He has a thoughtful face, one hand on his chin, and a phone in the other hand. RIGHT panel: a living room in a Mumbai flat; a woman in her 40s (teal salwar kameez, reading glasses pushed up on her head) holds a phone to her ear, her earlier angry face replaced by a sheepish smile, one hand on her chest as if apologizing; a speech bubble from the phone shows a small heart and a cricket bat; beside her on the wall hangs a framed photo of a boy in cricket whites holding a bat, and a small flyer with a cricket ball and stumps lies on the table. A dashed phone-call line arcs across the divider from his phone to hers. Soft evening lamp light, warm and friendly. Labels: "ANGRY INBOX" at the top of the left panel, "INVITED" at the top of the right panel.

key: A school principal in Chennai gives
name: ch18_principal_seats_by_marks
alt: A school principal calmly refuses an angry donor parent because science seats go by marks, and a month later the same parent happily helps at the school annual day.
scene: A wide scene inside a school principal's office in Chennai: a wooden desk with a brass bell, a stack of files, a small potted plant, and a ceiling fan; behind the desk a notice board shows a pinned merit list with ranked rows and a small star at the top. The principal (woman in her 50s, maroon silk saree, hair in a bun with jasmine flowers, spectacles) stands behind the desk with an open, calm, understanding face, one hand raised palm-up toward the parent and the other hand pointing at the merit list. Facing her on the left, a parent (man in his 50s, white shirt and veshti, gold watch, holding a thick folder of donation receipts) leans forward angrily with a red exclamation badge above him. A small inset bubble near the parent shows a commerce textbook and a smiling boy, the principal's kind words about his son. In the top-right corner, a rounded inset panel shows a month later: the same parent, now smiling, carrying a stack of chairs at a school annual day with a decorated stage, colourful bunting and children in costume. A dashed arrow runs from the office scene to the inset. Bright morning light through a window with a green shutter. Labels: "BY MARKS" above the notice board, "ANNUAL DAY" inside the top-right inset.

key: A housing society in Pune needs to
name: ch18_society_water_notice
alt: Residents of a housing society read a sympathetic notice about a one-day water shutdown, grumble and fill buckets, while a tanker stands by and an inset shows the week-long outage a burst pipe would cause.
scene: A wide scene at the ground floor of a Pune housing society: a four-storey apartment block with balconies and drying clothes, a society notice board near the gate, and a white water tanker parked on the right with a hose coiled on its side. The society secretary (man in his 60s, white kurta, spectacles, holding a pen and a clipboard) pins a notice to the board; the notice shows a water tap with a drop, a calendar page "SAT" and a small heart symbol to show the caring tone. In front of the board three residents: a young mother (yellow kurti) holding a toddler's hand, an elderly man with a walking stick, and a teenage boy, each carrying or filling plastic buckets at a common tap, with mild grumbling faces but nodding. Near the top-left a rusted pipe section is drawn with orange rust patches and a crack. In the top-right corner, a rounded inset bubble shows the alternative the secretary warns of: a burst pipe spraying water and a calendar with seven crossed-out days. A dashed arrow from the rusted pipe points to the inset. Early morning light, calm everyday mood. Labels: "ONE DAY" above the notice board, "ONE WEEK" inside the inset bubble.

key: A Kathak guru in Lucknow takes on
name: ch18_kathak_guru_ghungroo
alt: A Kathak guru admires a student's fancy anklets, suggests saving them for her first performance, and offers plain ghungroo for practice, which the student wears the next week.
scene: A wide scene inside a Kathak practice hall in Lucknow: a polished wooden floor, a large mirror on the back wall, a small framed picture of a dancing figure, a harmonium and a pair of tabla on a low mat on the right. The guru (woman in her 60s, cream cotton saree with a maroon border, grey hair in a bun, a dupatta over her shoulder) sits on a cushion, smiling warmly, holding up in one hand a pair of glittering, heavy designer anklets with many bells and coloured stones; her other hand offers a simple pair of plain brass ghungroo on a leather strap. Facing her, a teenage student (about 15, purple practice kurta, white churidar, long plait) stands with her hands clasped, listening, slightly shy. Between them on the floor sits an open decorated keepsake box where the fancy anklets will go, with a small star above it. Small sound lines rise from the plain ghungroo with a tiny musical note to show the footwork is heard clearly. In the top-right corner, a rounded inset shows next week: the student's feet in the plain ghungroo on the wooden floor, mid-step, with a green tick. Soft afternoon light through tall windows. Labels: "FOR THE STAGE" above the keepsake box, "FOR PRACTICE" above the plain ghungroo.

key: A star batsman calls the team manager
name: ch18_batsman_stiff_back
alt: A team manager sits beside a star batsman with a stiff back and agrees he can skip the match; after the warm-up the batsman decides to bat as long as the TV crew is told he is playing through pain.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a hotel room in the morning; a star batsman (man in his late 20s, team tracksuit, short beard) sits on the edge of the bed hunched forward, one hand pressed to his lower back, a worried face, a small red pain zigzag near his back; the team manager (man in his 50s, blazer with a team crest of a simple star, spectacles) sits on a chair facing him, leaning in with an open, calm, caring face, one hand gently raised; on the bedside table a phone and a glass of water; through the window a stadium floodlight tower. RIGHT panel: the practice nets beside the ground later that morning; the same batsman, now in white kit and pads, holds a bat and nods firmly with a determined face, a hand still on his back; beside him the manager nods; on the right edge a TV camera operator with a large shoulder camera and a reporter with a microphone wait by the boundary rope. A dashed arrow with a small stopwatch runs across the divider to show the warm-up between the two moments. Bright morning sun, green grass. Labels: "HEALTH FIRST" at the top of the left panel, "I WILL BAT" at the top of the right panel.

key: At any Indian family wedding, an aunt
name: ch18_wedding_aunt_knee
alt: At a family wedding, an aunt describing her knee operation is hurt when a young man brushes it off, and delighted when he asks how she manages the stairs.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, set at an Indian family wedding with marigold garlands, string lights and a decorated stage with a mandap in the background of both halves. The same aunt (woman in her 60s, bright pink silk saree, gold bangles, spectacles, holding a walking stick, a beige knee bandage visible above her ankle) stands next to the same young man (late 20s, blue kurta, holding a plate of food). Above the aunt a thought bubble shows her story: a hospital bed, a surgeon's mask and a row of stitches on a knee. LEFT panel: the young man looks away at his phone, waving a hand dismissively; his small speech bubble shows two identical knee icons with an equals sign to show 'very common'; the aunt's face drops, mouth turned down, a small grey cloud above her. RIGHT panel: the young man leans in, plate lowered, eyes on her with concern; his speech bubble shows a small staircase with a question mark; the aunt beams, one hand on his arm, and a small heart floats between them; a little inset beside them shows her now listening while he talks, to show she will hear his news afterwards. Warm evening light from the string lights, festive mood. Labels: "BRUSH OFF" at the top of the left panel, "LISTEN" at the top of the right panel.
